channel.title: Said & Checked: District of Columbia — AskAmerica
channel.description: What officeholders said each day from or about District of Columbia, and which statements government data supports, contradicts or rules out.

item.title: Said & Checked, District of Columbia, 2026-11-18: none false or contradicted, 4 unsettled (Melanie Stansbury, Jamie Raskin, Bruce Westerman)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Melanie Stansbury, U.S. Representative from New Mexico: “In contrast to how the current administration is attempting to plaster Washington, D.C., with vanity projects requested by the President in violation of current law” Unsettled. Judge Leon and a D.C. Circuit panel found the White House ballroom likely unlawful without congressional authorization. The Supreme Court stayed that injunction 5-4 on standing grounds without deciding legality, and a certiorari petition is pending. Suits over the planned arch are undecided. No final ruling or GAO finding was found. Court holdings are as reported by NPR and SCOTUSblog.
  • Jamie Raskin, U.S. Representative from Maryland: “That recommendation has yet to be transmitted to Congress, which has slowed down our work.” Unsettled. The AP reported in January 2026 that the National Capital Memorial Advisory Commission recommended Area I placement in September 2024 and that the Interior Secretary must endorse it before it goes to Congress. No record was found showing whether it has since been transmitted.
  • Bruce Westerman, U.S. Representative from Arkansas: “Today, the network consists of over 200 sites” Unsettled. The National Park Service says the African American Civil Rights Network's authorization expired Jan. 8, 2025, and its pages publish no total site count, so 'over 200' was neither confirmed nor ruled out.

item.title: Said & Checked, District of Columbia, 2026-11-16: none false or contradicted, 2 unsettled (Donald Trump)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Donald Trump, President of the United States: “It is in a terrible state of disrepair, as anybody can see by just looking at the pictures that are now circulating all over the Country, and in the Court” Unsettled. FOX 5 DC reports that a court filing by the superintendent of the National Mall and Memorial Parks says the former operator did not keep up agreed maintenance and found several areas of the course "to either be deteriorating or needing work". The filing itself could not be read directly, and no National Park Service condition assessment or deferred-maintenance figure for the course was found. Whether that amounts to a "terrible state of disrepair" is a judgment the record read does not settle.
  • Donald Trump, President of the United States: “They don't call it Trash Island for no reason!” Unsettled. City Cast DC reports that, according to an Oct. 9 Washington Post story, National Park Service crews had used the name for "an overgrown central area of debris and invasive vegetation" in the park; that Post story could not be read directly. City Cast also reports that the D.C. Public Library's People's Archive "did not find a record where East Potomac Park had been referred to as 'Trash Island'" and that a search of the Post's archive found no earlier use of the name for the park. Only the name was checked.
